mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in three months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and boosts consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.5% in three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 5% over two months signals increased demand for housing and related goods, which boosts economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% in two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals increased supply-side activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the months where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals increased consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the months where RSAFS increased by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure, which increases the cost of capital and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the same quarter, it signals strong economic growth and a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 0.5% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the quarters where GDPC1 increased by more than 0.5% and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3%.
